outcome: preeclampsia and eclampsia superimposed on pre-existing hypertension
cohort: The study included 2,596 pregnant women from the HCUP-NIS database, comprising 1,978 women with focal epilepsy and 618 with generalized epilepsy.
finding: Women with focal epilepsy had significantly increased rates of cesarean sections compared to those with generalized epilepsy, while other pregnancy and neonatal outcomes did not differ significantly.
mod_finding: Focal epilepsy was associated with increased rates of cesarean sections compared to generalized epilepsy.
